output.summary: KEP-3140 adds an optional `.spec.timeZone` field to the CronJob resource so users can set the IANA time zone name used to schedule Jobs, instead of relying on the kube-controller-manager's local time zone. Empty or unset keeps the current behavior.
output.rationale: CronJob schedules were evaluated in the time zone of kube-controller-manager, which users could not control per resource. Earlier objections centered on needing an external tz database, but Go 1.15's time/tzdata lets the database be embedded in the binary. With CronJob now GA, the proposal adds the field to satisfy the original request.

alternatives.option: Specify the time zone as an offset to UTC
alternatives.why_not: The design says using the name instead seems more user friendly.

alternatives.option: Keep relying on the kube-controller-manager time zone
alternatives.why_not: The proposal exists to satisfy the original request for time zone support, which the status quo does not provide; the sources do not give a further reason.

evidence.quote: Starting from [golang 1.15](https://go.dev/doc/go1.15) `time/tzdata` package can be embedded in the binary thus removing the requirement for external database.
Add the field `.spec.timeZone` to the CronJob resource. The cronjob controller will take the field into account when scheduling the next Job run.
In case the field is not specified or is empty, the controller will maintain the current behavior, which is to rely on the time zone of the kube-controller-manager process.
Another approach was to specify time zone as an offset to UTC, but using the name instead seems more user friendly.
